sources_considered.why: Primary policy document reporting business concerns about regulatory fragmentation. It supplies context, not a measured causal effect.
Primary research establishes the environmental cost of model training, but does not test regulatory harmonisation.
Journal version of the same research; the dated arXiv record was used instead of assigning an unsupported exact journal publication day.

evidence_items.publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
evidence_items.explanation: The March white paper reports a business rationale for compatible international rules; the cited page is its August-updated version. Stakeholder expectations do not establish measured interoperability gains or avoided model training.

This study estimates the environmental footprint of BLOOM training and deployment. It supports the premise that training has environmental costs, but does not show that common national rules prevent additional training.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved study compares otherwise similar deployments under harmonised and divergent national requirements.
No retrieved evidence establishes how much country-specific training common standards would avoid.
The sources do not establish the complete link from shared standards to lower emissions.
